newsitem.title: UK: Eurobourses mixed, nervous over Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Eurobourses mixed, nervous over Wall Street.

text.p: European bourses put in a mixed performance in early trade on Thursday with investors jittery after renewed fears about interest rates caused a sharp fall on Wall Street.
On currency markets, the dollar was slightly stronger but traders anxiously awaited U.S. consumer price figures due at 1330 GMT for clues on the health of the American economy.
London, Europe's biggest stock market, made a robust start, climbing 0.4 percent although business was light and investors edgy because of the Dow Jones industrials' one percent drop on Wednesday.

Stocks and bonds in New York had tumbled on renewed fears of an interest rate hike and fresh worries about corporate earnings. The Dow had in fact fallen by two percent before recovering some poise at the close.

London's buoyant start hid a fragile mood and investors were nervous that another dip in Wall Street later in the day could signal the end of New York's bull run, already damaged by the U.S. Federal Reserve's warning about "irrational market exuberance".
"We'll just drift around until we see how the Dow opens," a trader said. "I don't really expect any serious buying or selling until we see whether or not the Dow can spring back."
In Frankfurt, which ended sharply down on Wednesday, stocks edged up in early transaction as the steady dollar helped dispel worries over New York's weak close.
"It looks like there is a bit of life back in the market," said one dealer.

The stronger dollar helped boost some chemical sector shares because of enhanced export prospects, with Hoechst attracting interest after announcing that it would sell off its specialty chemicals business to Swiss group Clariant.
In Paris, stocks slipped a few points in early trade, confounding expectations for a rebound from Wednesday steep fall. "The market is fragile," a trader said.
On the currency front, the dollar strengthened a little against the mark and the yen as some of the stock and bond markets regained their poise overnight after Wednesday's drop.
Traders and analysts said it was difficult to discern any clear market trends but volatility would persist before the holiday season.

"Everyone is just getting a little edgy in these markets given the time of the year and it's hard to see an end to the volatility in the very short term," said Ian Gunner, economist at Chase Investment Bank.

But for the braver market players who are still prepared to take a slightly longer-term view, a resumption of the themes of a higher dollar against European currencies and an independently strong sterling are still the best bets, dealers said.

Currency markets, however, are expected to remain nervous this week before the weekend European Union summit and the last minute horse-trading between governments over a post-monetary union budgetary stability pact.
European finance ministers will meet at 1600 GMT on Thursday to make final preparations for the summit.
CURRENCIES AT 1015 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 113.21 yen and 1.5440 marks against 112.92 and 1.5412 in late European business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1015 GMT
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares was 14.7 points higher at 3,997.2
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index was down 2.46 at 2,210.82.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt climbed 8.64 points to to 2,849.69.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold opened at $368.50 an ounce, compared to Wednesday's close of $368.65. Silver was marginally lower at $4.82, down one cent.
